our_interpretation: Marcus tentatively describes an apparent failure to follow safeguards. The word “apparently” qualifies the factual proposition.
“Don’t always” concerns occasional failures; it does not assert that all agents fail or that failures are frequent.

Treating this as a firm assertion that documented failures occurred would remove his explicit uncertainty. Under the supplied exclusion for hedged claims, this wording is not eligible for a binary factual assessment.
criteria.support_condition: Not applicable under the exclusion for hedged claims. Documented incidents could substantiate the concern, but would not justify silently replacing the tentative wording with a firm assertion.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Not applicable under the exclusion for hedged claims. Successful agent runs would also not disprove an occasional-failure proposition.
